text: In the spring of fourteen fifty-three, a city that had stood for eleven hundred years was about to fall. Its walls had turned back army after army. Its emperor had perhaps seven thousand men to hold them. Facing him: tens of thousands of soldiers, a twenty-one-year-old sultan, and a very large cannon. Now, you would think a thousand years of history might buy you a little more time. But history, as it turns out, has never once accepted a loyalty card.
